portrait-dennick-ashe.webp.prompt:
A character portrait in a painterly fantasy-realism style, the classic CRPG portrait look: head and shoulders, three-quarter view, looking at the viewer, dramatic soft key light, a dark, softly painted background. No text, lettering, borders or frames.

Art bible for the Brannock system. Palette: #c8661e, #4a3a33, #7a5a46, #5e5953, #1d4f7a, #d8cba8. Lighting: Low orange starlight from a dim sun, and sodium lamps that turn every shadow brown. Welding arcs flash blue-white in the gloom. Refinery flares throw moving orange light across grey surfaces. Architecture: Modular boxes and drums welded to girders or bolted to bare rock. Hab rings are clamped onto cliffs and asteroids. Walkways are added wherever someone needed one, and ladders and cable runs cross every wall. Materials: Rust-streaked plate, weld seams left visible, riveted patches in mismatched greys and browns. Cable, chain, scored steel, stained concrete, and cracked sealant gone yellow. Mood: Tired, practical, and warm at the edges. It is a place where hard work is done and nobody is impressed by it. Design language: Ironhull design is welded, modular, rusted and patched. Every structure has been repaired many times, and the repairs are never hidden. Sodium-lamp orange marks everything that is lit, and hab rings are bolted straight onto rock.

Dennick Ashe, tug pilot, at Cinder Deep (Cinder). A lean man in his thirties with a sunburned neck and sharp eyes, in a flight jacket with the sleeves cut off. A long burn scar runs up his left forearm. He keeps a cold pipe in his teeth.

Who they are: He flies ore from the lift head to the refinery and back. He knows the routes better than the charts do, and trusts neither.

Their people: People in Brannock measure each other by what they can fix. A good welder gets a drink bought for her, and a clean-handed visitor gets a look. They speak shortly, swear mildly, and tease newcomers with the old names, rusters and rockheads, until the newcomer answers in kind. Then the teasing stops. Outsiders are tolerated if they pay, and trusted if they turn up with the right part at the right time. Nothing is thrown away. A broken thing is a future patch, and a dead ship is a shopping list.
